subtitle: Ray-Traced Geometry Reverb
tagline: Builds a reverb from a 3D shape: rays travel through a closed mesh from an emitter to a listener, and its scale, materials, radiation, and positions shape the space you hear.

body.lead: TB Geometry Reverb turns a 3D shape into a room. It traces sound rays through a closed mesh from an emitter (E) to a listener (L); the paths that reach the listener, the surface materials, the scale of the mesh, and the air temperature form an acoustic snapshot of the space, and an eight-line feedback delay network adds the dense tail.

body.p: Choose a built-in model or import your own OBJ or FBX mesh, assign materials to its surfaces, and place the emitter and listener inside it. `SCALE` sets the size, `TEMP / HF` the air, `RADIATION` how the emitter radiates, and `MIX` the equal-power dry/wet balance. The view shows the mesh with the ray paths that contribute to the sound.

ul: Ray-traced acoustic snapshot with 64 direction bins and three ray-quality levels
13 built-in models, from a cube to a trefoil knot and an auditorium, plus OBJ and FBX import
Closed-mesh validation with live status and an escaped-ray readout
Surface materials with absorption and scattering, per face or for all surfaces
Sphere or cone radiation with a 10 to 180° cone
Emitter and listener position and orientation in 3D
SCALE from 0.25 to 20×, air temperature from −271 to 100 °C
Calculated pre-delay, triangle count, and mid-frequency RT60
30 factory presets, user presets, undo, and redo

note.title: About this manual
text: This manual describes TB Geometry Reverb 1.0.0 for Windows (VST3). There is no macOS build at the time of writing.

ol: Insert TB Geometry Reverb on a track or an effects return. The default is a 2 m cube at SCALE 1.00×, with the emitter at X −0.20 and the listener at X 0.20, TEMP 20 °C, and MIX 35%.
Choose a starting point from the preset bar {{1}}, or pick a model in GEOMETRY {{5}}.
Set the size with `SCALE` {{9}} and the balance with `MIX` {{12}}.
Choose a material in SURFACE {{7}} and press APPLY ALL.
Switch between EMITTER and LISTENER {{13}} and place them with `LOCATE` {{14}} and `ROTATE` {{15}}. Wait until the status line {{4}} reads READY.

body.p: In the view, the selected point shows coloured X, Y, and Z handles. The scale bar under the model shows its size, and the line under the side panel shows the speed of sound (343 m/s at 20 °C).

rows: Scales the mesh coordinates before path timing. Larger values make a bigger space with longer paths.
Air temperature. It sets the speed of sound and changes the high-frequency (HF) damping.
An additional effect amount that pushes the space harder; the DRIVE presets use it. Raise it gradually.
SPHERE emits through all 64 direction bins; CONE focuses them into a cone.
Cone apex angle. Available only when RADIATION is CONE.
How many rays are traced (4096 at NORM in the picture). Higher quality is more detailed and takes longer to calculate.
Position of the emitter or listener, relative to the mesh. Both must stay inside the closed mesh.
azimuth −180 to 180°, elevation −89 to 89°, roll −180 to 180° · 0°

Orientation of the emitter or listener. Listener angles are measured from the direction of the emitter, so 0° faces the source. Roll does nothing for the emitter, because a cone is rotationally symmetric.

body.p: The following host parameters are stored in presets and the project but do not appear on the panel shown above.

rows: Spin X, Spin Y, Spin Z
Rotation speed of the mesh around each axis.
An additional grain effect amount, used in several factory presets.

ul: Built-in models: Tetrahedron, Cube, Sphere, Torus, Twisted Torus, Trefoil Knot, Superellipsoid, Harmonic Shell, Spiked Shell, Hyperboloid, Corrugated Drum, Capsule, and Auditorium.
IMPORT MESH loads a Wavefront OBJ or FBX file in the background. Files must be 1 byte to 64 MiB, with up to 250,000 vertices and 500,000 triangles.
Only a closed manifold mesh can produce a new acoustic snapshot. Open or non-manifold meshes are shown but not simulated, and self-intersections are not tested.
The emitter and the listener must both stay inside the rotated closed mesh; otherwise the status line shows BLOCKED.
PRE-DELAY, TRIANGLES, and RT60 MID are calculated from the current snapshot.
Factory materials include Concrete, Concrete Block (Painted), Wood, Glass, Metal, and Curtain.
The readout under the material shows A (absorption at low, mid, and high frequencies), R (reflection), and S (scattering).
APPLY FACE assigns the material to the selected face; APPLY ALL assigns it to every surface. A mesh can use up to 256 material snapshots.

The material menu also offers IMPORT JSON, LIBRARY, OPEN USER FOLDER, and RESCAN. User materials are .tbmaterial.json files with absorption and scattering coefficients from 0 to 1; up to 255 user material files are scanned.

body.p: Step through presets with the arrows, or open the list to choose a factory or user preset. SAVE stores the current settings, including the mesh and its materials, as a .tbgeometry file. Undo and Redo step through recent changes. In the table, TEMP is the air temperature and Quality the ray quality.
Starting points for common jobs. Adjust them by ear.

recipes.title: Small studio
recipes.use: A short, natural room for vocals and instruments.
steps: Raise SCALE slightly if the room feels too tight.

recipes.title: Concrete hall
recipes.use: A large, hard space for drums or cinematic hits.
steps: Use an absorbent material such as Curtain if the tail gets too bright.

recipes.title: Directed source
recipes.use: A beam of sound aimed into the space.
steps: Turn the emitter with ROTATE to aim the beam.

recipes.title: Abstract space
steps: Use DRAFT while editing and HIGH for the final sound.

First release: a geometry-based reverb with mesh import, closed-mesh validation, and emitter and listener position checks; a 64-direction snapshot ray model with three ray-quality levels and an eight-line FDN pass; material, scale, and radiation-pattern control; state, preset, and host-state handling for snapshot calculation.
